| [LIT-763](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-763.md) | Erwin: A Tree-based Hierarchical Transformer for Large-scale Physical Systems | Zhdanov et al. (2025), [ARXIV-2502.17019](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17019) — Erwin. Build a ball tree over an irregular point set so that every ball at a level holds the same number of points in contiguous memory, then run full self-attention inside each ball, coarsen and refine through the tree in a U-Net, and alternate with a tree built on a rotated copy of the cloud so balls exchange information. Runtime fits n^1.054. Best on cosmology at large training sets, on EAGLE turbulence (3× faster and 8× less memory than EAGLE's own model), and on ShapeNet-Car; a clear failure on the Airfoil PDE mesh. | Active |
| [LIT-812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-812.md) | E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks | Satorras, Hoogeboom, Welling (ICML 2021), [ARXIV-2102.09844](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09844). A message-passing layer that also carries a coordinate per node: messages see only squared distances, and coordinates move along a weighted sum of relative position vectors, which is E(n)-equivariant in any dimension without spherical harmonics. On a 3D charged 5-body system it cuts position MSE 32% against the next model (0.0071 vs 0.0104). On QM9 it does not update coordinates, which makes it an invariant distance GNN, and it is competitive rather than best. | Active |
| [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md) | GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting | Lam et al. (Science 2023), [ARXIV-2212.12794](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12794). A 36.7M-parameter encode-process-decode GNN on an icosahedral multi-mesh, trained on 39 years of ERA5 to step the global 0.25° state six hours ahead, rolled out to 10 days. Against ECMWF's HRES, each scored on its own analysis, it has lower RMSE on 90.3% of 1,380 variable-level-lead-time targets (89.9% significantly). Most losses are at 50 hPa, which with the levels above it carries 0.66% of the training loss weight. Deterministic only, and its MSE training blurs long-lead forecasts; with both models optimally blurred it still wins 88.0%. | Active |
| [LIT-822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-822.md) | Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks | Pfaff, Fortunato, Sanchez-Gonzalez, Battaglia (ICLR 2021), [ARXIV-2010.03409](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03409). MeshGraphNets: an encode-process-decode graph network that passes messages along simulation-mesh edges and, for deforming bodies, along world-space proximity edges, trained on one-step targets with input noise and rolled out for hundreds of steps. It beats a grid U-Net, a GCN and the particle model GNS on cloth, plates and 2D flows, and can learn the remesher's sizing field. The quoted 11–290× speedup is a GPU model against CPU solvers; on the same CPU it is 4–22×. | Active |
| [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md) | SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions | Schütt et al. (NeurIPS 2017), [ARXIV-1706.08566](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.08566). Message passing over atoms whose filters are generated by a network from interatomic distances, so the energy is rotation-invariant and smooth, and forces taken as its negative gradient are energy-conserving. QM9 U0 MAE 0.31 kcal/mol at 110k training molecules. On MD17 with 1,000 configurations, training on energies and forces cuts force MAE 17–46× against energies alone (benzene 14.12 → 0.31 kcal/mol/Å), and beats energy-only training on 50,000 on forces. The kernel baseline GDML still has the lower force error on 6 of 8 molecules. | Active |
| [LIT-828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-828.md) | MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields | Batatia, Kovács, Simm, Ortner, Csányi (NeurIPS 2022), [ARXIV-2206.07697](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.07697). MACE builds each message as a symmetric tensor product of a neighbor sum, so one layer carries up to four-body correlations at roughly pairwise cost, and two layers suffice where two-body equivariant models need four to six. On 3BPA at 1200 K its force RMSE is 62.0 meV/Å against NequIP's 76.2, at about a quarter of NequIP's latency in the authors' code. On aspirin, raising body order steepens the learning curve (slopes −0.33, −0.51, −0.64) and, at body order four, adding equivariant features does not (−0.64, −0.63, −0.64). | Active |
| [LIT-829](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-829.md) | Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry | Gilmer, Schoenholz, Riley, Vinyals, Dahl (ICML 2017), [ARXIV-1704.01212](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01212). Message Passing Neural Networks name the common form of eight earlier graph models: T rounds of messages summed over neighbors, a node update, and a permutation-invariant readout. An MPNN with edge-network messages, set2set readout and explicit hydrogens reaches chemical accuracy on 11 of 13 QM9 targets, with an average error ratio of 0.68 against 1.35 for the best hand-engineered baseline. That is one random split, with no repeated runs. | Active |
| [LIT-832](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-832.md) | E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials | Batzner et al. (Nature Communications 2022), [ARXIV-2101.03164](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03164). NequIP: a message-passing interatomic potential whose features are O(3) tensors up to order l, combined by Clebsch–Gordan tensor products with spherical- harmonic filters, with forces as the gradient of the energy. On MD17 with 1,000 configurations, aspirin force MAE 8.2 meV/Å against SchNet's 58.5. The same network with only l = 0 features scores 41.9 on revised MD17, and 12.9 at l = 1. The equivariant variants also show a steeper log-log learning curve than the invariant one, on water and aspirin, read from figures. "1000× fewer data" is a force-error comparison against an older, non-smooth DeepMD; on energies DeepMD stays ahead. | Active |
